after: ## 1. The nature, existence and persistence of poverty
alt: Three studies in sequence: Rowntree’s absolute poverty line (1899), Townsend’s relative deprivation index (1979) and Mack and Lansley’s consensual approach (1985), with definitions of absolute and relative poverty and the UK’s 60% of median income measure.
caption: Measures of poverty moved from survival needs to what is normal in a society.

after: ## 1. The nature, existence and persistence of poverty
alt: Cultural explanations from Lewis and Murray blame values and welfare dependency; structural explanations from Townsend and Marxists blame low pay, unemployment and capitalism. Rodman, MacDonald and Marsh, and Shildrick challenge the cultural view.
caption: Is poverty caused by values or by blocked opportunities?

after: ## 2. The distribution of poverty, wealth and income
alt: Income is shown as a flow of money over time and wealth as a stock of assets. Wealth is more unequal because it builds up and is inherited. Below, groups more likely to be poor and explanations by gender, ethnicity and class.
caption: Wealth accumulates, so it is far more unequal than income.

alt: Welfare pluralism combines four providers: the state (from the Beveridge Report to Universal Credit), the private sector (pensions and insurance), the voluntary sector (charities such as food banks) and informal care by family and neighbours.
caption: Welfare comes from the state, private, voluntary and informal sectors together.

alt: Social democrats favour redistribution and universal benefits; the New Right sees welfare creating dependency; Marxists see it stabilising capitalism; feminists see it relying on women’s unpaid care.
caption: Each perspective sees a different purpose and problem in welfare.

after: ## 4. Organisation and control of the labour process
alt: Braverman argues managers use Taylorism and machinery to deskill and control workers; Blauner argues advancing technology makes work more skilled with more discretion. Gallie’s survey found polarisation rather than widespread deskilling.
caption: The effect of technology depends on how it is used and the type of work.

after: ## 4. Organisation and control of the labour process
alt: Two rings: a skilled, secure core of staff surrounded by a peripheral group on temporary or part-time terms. Side panels show Piore and Sabel’s flexible specialisation and the criticism that flexibility means insecurity.
caption: The flexible firm keeps a secure core and an insecure periphery.

after: ## 5. The significance of work and worklessness, including globalisation
alt: Paid employment at the centre with five latent functions around it: time structure, social contact, shared purpose, status and identity, and regular activity.
caption: Unemployment harms people by removing the hidden benefits of work as well as the wage.
